luke.10.p1.b1.text: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.

luke.10.p1.b2.text: “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.

luke.10.p1.b3.text: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.

luke.10.p2.b1.text: Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.

luke.10.p2.b2.text: Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.

luke.10.p2.b4.text: If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him;

luke.10.p3.b1.text: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages.

luke.10.p3.b2.text: Do not move around from house to house.

luke.10.p3.b3.text: ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’

luke.10.p4.b1.text: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,

luke.10.p4.b2.text: ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you.

luke.10.p4.b3.text: Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’

luke.10.p4.b4.text: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.

luke.10.p5.b1.text: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida!

luke.10.p5.b2.text: For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

luke.10.p5.b3.text: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!

luke.10.p5.b4.text: Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”

luke.10.p6.b1.text: “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”

luke.10.p6.b2.text: “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.

luke.10.p6.b3.text: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.

luke.10.p6.b4.text: Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

luke.10.p7.b1.text: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared,

luke.10.p7.b2.text: “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.

luke.10.p7.b3.text: “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.

luke.10.p7.b4.text: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”

luke.10.p8.b1.text: “Teacher, … what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

luke.10.p8.b2.text: “What is written in the Law? … How do you read it?”

luke.10.p8.b3.text: “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”

luke.10.p8.b4.text: “You have answered correctly, … Do this and you will live.”

luke.10.p9.b2.text: “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers.

luke.10.p9.b3.text: They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.

luke.10.p9.b4.text: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

luke.10.p10.b1.text: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.

luke.10.p10.b2.text: But when a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion.

luke.10.p11.b1.text: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine.

luke.10.p11.b2.text: Then he put him on his own animal,

luke.10.p11.b3.text: brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

luke.10.p12.b1.text: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper.

luke.10.p12.b2.text: ‘Take care of him, … and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’

luke.10.p13.b1.text: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”

luke.10.p14.b1.text: … Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.

luke.10.p14.b2.text: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.

luke.10.p14.b3.text: “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”

luke.10.p15.b2.text: “you are worried and upset about many things. But only one thing is necessary.

luke.10.p15.b3.text: Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”
